From Byzantine Greek καλόγερος (kalógeros, “monk”). The meanings ‘ergot, charcoal’ are based on a monk’s black habit. Doublet of kallogjer.

From Byzantine Greek κασοῦλα (kasoûla), from Latin casula (“hooded cloak”). Doublet of kaçule. Compare also Romanian căciulă. Attested in 1417 (Catasto Veneto di Scutari) as "Chisolichochi" (i.e. Kësolëkoqi, modern Kësulëkuqi, "bearing a red riding hood", masc.).
From Byzantine Greek λιβάδιον (libádion).
From Byzantine Greek μαγγοῦνα (mangoûna), μαγκοῦνα (mankoûna), an obscure word, also found mingled with Latin cicūta as μαγγοῦτα (mangoûta), μαγκοῦτα (mankoûta).
From Byzantine Greek μοῦλα (moûla), from Vulgar Latin *mūla (compare Old French mule (“abomasum”), Aromanian mură).
Borrowed from Byzantine Greek πατάσσω (patássō, “to strike”).

parole.significato: pastry made out of several layers, filled with cheese, meat, etc.

Borrowed from Byzantine Greek τηγάνιν (tēgánin), Koine Greek τηγάνιον (tēgánion). Cognate with Sicilian tiganu.
